title: LET YOUR WORD BE YOUR BOND

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Moses said to the heads of the tribes of Israel: "This is what the LORD commands: When a man makes a vow to the LORD or takes an oath to obligate himself by a pledge, he must not break his word but must do everything he said." - Num 30:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This chapter opens with a clear and weighty principle: when a person makes a vow to the Lord, they must keep it. To break one's word was a serious matter before God. A vow was not a casual promise to be forgotten when convenient; it was a binding commitment that had to be fulfilled. God takes our words seriously.

We live in a world where words are often cheap. Promises are made lightly and broken easily. Commitments are treated as flexible, to be honoured only as long as they suit us. But God's standard is different. He calls His people to be those whose word can be trusted, whose yes means yes and whose no means no.

There is something deeply important about integrity here. When we make a promise, whether to God or to others, keeping it reflects the faithfulness of the God we serve. A person of integrity does what they said they would do, even when it becomes costly or difficult. Our reliability honours the Lord.

Jesus taught that we should be so truthful that our simple word is enough, without needing elaborate oaths to back it up (Matt 5:37). And the deepest comfort is that God Himself always keeps His word; every promise He has made is faithful and true (2 Cor 1:20). As those who belong to the faithful God, let us be people whose word can always be trusted.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you keep your promises, even when it becomes costly?
2. How does your faithfulness to your word reflect God's character?
3. Where might God be calling you to greater integrity in your commitments?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, make me a person of my word, whose promises can be trusted. Help me to reflect Your faithfulness by keeping my commitments, even when they become difficult or costly. Amen.
